tm_reasoning: Chicago (Dfa) is heating-dominant annually; the office runs heating days at 21.1 °C and setback nights at 15.6 °C. At pos4 (just behind the interior gypsum), the interface temperature will swing roughly with the indoor air because only ~0.10 m²K/W separates the PCM from the room.

With a 4 °C phase band, Tm=18 °C gives [16–20 °C]. In winter weekdays the interface will be above 20 °C during occupied hours (~21.1 °C) and fall to ≤16 °C overnight (setback 15.6 °C), ensuring daily melt–freeze cycling and high latent utilization when heating loads are largest. [case_Harbin]

Coupling effectiveness: at pos4 the indoor-side resistance is ~0.10 m²K/W vs >1.7 m²K/W to the exterior, so most latent heat directly offsets space-conditioning of the room; interior-adjacent PCM yields greater indoor interaction and energy benefit. [0c4b2e474e2990e946d266a1a5391b92__text__0001]

Summer cycling is less critical for annual minimum energy in Chicago. With AC at 23.9 °C, an interior-adjacent PCM set at 18 °C will often melt by day but may not fully refreeze nightly; however, heating-season savings dominate the year.

Independent cross-check: in a severe-cold case (Harbin), the interior PCM optimum for winter was ~18 °C, near the heating setpoint but low enough to guarantee overnight solidification—consistent with this choice for a cold/mixed climate. [case_Harbin]
Material compatibility: candidate organic PCMs around 18 °C have latent heat ~200 kJ/kg, matching the task’s PCM parameterization. [3fc0212289cc39ffae6bae56c80890b2__table__0001]
final.joint_rationale: Placing the PCM at the insulation/inner-gypsum interface maximizes coupling to the room (minimal indoor-side resistance) so latent exchanges directly reduce HVAC energy. Choosing Tm=18 °C aligns the melt–freeze band with winter day/night indoor temperatures, guaranteeing daily cycling when heating loads dominate Chicago’s annual energy. This pairing optimizes the product of cycle depth and indoor-coupling, outperforming outward positions that cycle more but are insulated from the room.
reasoning_chain: Wall resistances from outside: stucco 25 mm (R≈0.035), outer gypsum 16 mm (R≈0.10), NoMass insulation (R=1.65), inner gypsum 16 mm (R≈0.10). Total ≈1.88 m²K/W. At pos4, indoor-side R≈0.10 while outdoor-side R>1.7, so the PCM is strongly coupled to the room (heat preferentially flows to the interior).

Chicago (Dfa) has hot summers and cold winters; the small office holds 21.1 °C (heat) and 23.9 °C (cool) in occupied hours, with setbacks to 15.6 °C (heat) and 29.4 °C (cool) off-hours. This creates large winter indoor swings at night that a near-interior PCM can exploit.

Interface envelopes by position: pos0 sees the largest swings but is thermally decoupled from the room by the whole wall; pos1/pos2 are still outside-biased; pos3 (mid-insulation) has ~symmetric coupling; pos4 closely tracks indoor air and sees the winter day (~21 °C) to night (~16 °C) swing needed for cycling.

Phase-cycling test at pos4: with Tm=18 °C (band 16–20), winter weekdays exceed 20 °C during occupied heating and drop to ~16 °C or lower at night—enabling full daily melt/solidify. Tm=20 or 22 °C would not reliably exceed their upper band edges (~22 or 24 °C) during heating days at 21.1 °C, risking under-cycling.

Effectiveness (position-coupling) criterion: interior-adjacent PCM increases interaction with indoor temperature fluctuations and yields larger energy impact than exterior placement for annual performance—reported innermost layer outperforms outermost for total energy; mechanism: proximity enhances latent utilization. [0c4b2e474e2990e946d266a1a5391b92__text__0001]

Placement guidance for cold/mixed climates indicates interior or middle layers provide better balanced or heating-favorable performance, aligning with a near-interior choice here. [6c1a02ab446c7b043b049640620f1469__table__0014]

Climate-matched winter Tm: a severe-cold case found interior PCM with Tm≈18 °C optimal for heating season—close to indoor heating setpoints but low enough to ensure night solidification—supporting Tm=18 °C at an interior-adjacent position. [case_Harbin]

Rule check (cooling-dominated external PCM): studies favoring exterior PCM target hot, cooling-dominated contexts; that mechanism does not transfer to Chicago’s heating-weighted annual objective, so exterior placements are deprioritized here. [rule_1]

PCM properties: 18–30 °C variants with latent ≈200 kJ/kg are common; selecting the 18 °C option matches the provided PCM parameter set and ensures robust winter cycling at pos4. [3fc0212289cc39ffae6bae56c80890b2__table__0001]

alternatives.why_not_preferred: Mid-insulation (pos3) offers better cycling than pos4, but only ~50/50 coupling to indoor vs outdoor; with heating dominating in Chicago, this dilutes latent benefits compared to interior-adjacent placement. Also, Tm=20 °C risks insufficient daytime melting during heating (21.1 °C < 22 °C upper band edge). Interior/middle guidance favors interior for heating; Harbin’s winter optimum (18 °C, interior) supports a lower Tm at a more interior position.

Exterior placement with high Tm cycles well in summer but is largely decoupled from indoor air by the wall insulation, yielding weak annual savings and no winter benefit. External-PCM rules mainly apply to hot, cooling-dominated contexts, not Chicago’s mixed/heating-weighted profile.

At the heating setpoint (21.1 °C), Tm=22 °C (band 20–24) would often fail to reach the 24 °C upper threshold during occupied hours, limiting melt and reducing latent utilization. Evidence emphasizes matching Tm to indoor operating temperatures and ensuring full daily cycling; winter-focused interior studies favor slightly lower Tm (≈18 °C).
